correctness.rationale: For every labeled fair tournament, the unique-dominating-vertex score identity is exact. The root-of-unity identity holds for all d mod 4, orientations factor independently over complete-graph edges, all nonconstant vertex characters annihilate, and elementary phase arithmetic gives positive 2^{-floor((n-1)/2)}. The verifier compares independent arc pattern counts at n=3..6 and uses integer Gaussian arithmetic through n=100; finite computation is not claimed as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The complete-graph character sum gives a signed, all-orders parity census; the inspected classical literature concerns ordinary moments, asymptotic normality, five-cycles, or fixed-small-count generating functions. None of the inspected exact claims implies this alternating all-count sum without substantial new summation. Priority is provisional, with the inaccessible 1940 original explicitly flagged.
residual_risks: The foundational Kendall--Smith (1940) original full text could not be inspected under available access; it may contain a signed enumeration beyond the reported four moments.
Scattered older score-sequence enumeration literature may contain an equivalent parity identity under alternative nomenclature. Negative searches establish no uniqueness.

value.rationale: Circular triads measure rank inconsistency. Their exact parity bias is an all-order signed enumeration invisible to a finite set of low ordinary moments or Gaussian asymptotics. The precise decay rate and equality between adjacent odd/even orders follow from a structural two-character cancellation; this gives a motivated binary benchmark rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
